wlc: אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: ΑΣΜΑ ἀσμάτων, ὅ ἐστιν τῷ Σαλωμών.
vulg: osculetur me osculo oris sui quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino
clem: [ Sponsa Osculetur me osculo oris sui; quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino,
kjv: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: Φιλησάτω με ἀπὸ φιλημάτων στόματος αὐτοῦ· ὅτι ἀγαθοὶ μαστοί σου ὑπὲρ οἶνον,
vulg: fraglantia unguentis optimis oleum effusum nomen tuum ideo adulescentulae dilexerunt te
clem: fragrantia unguentis optimis. Oleum effusum nomen tuum; ideo adolescentul dilexerunt te.
kjv: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: ³καὶ ὀσμὴ μύρων σου ὑπέρ πάντα τὰ 3 ἀρώματα· μύρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου. διὰ τοῦτο νεάνιδες ἠγάπησάν σε,
vulg: trahe me post te curremus introduxit me rex in cellaria sua exultabimus et laetabimur in te memores uberum tuorum super vinum recti diligunt te
clem: Chorus Adolescentularum Trahe me, post te curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum. Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua; exsultabimus et ltabimur in te, memores uberum tuorum super vinum. Recti diligunt te.
kjv: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: εἴλκυσάν σε· ὀπίσω σου εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρσων σου δραμομεν. εἰσήνεγκέν με ὁ βασιλεὺς εἰς τὸ ταμεῖον αὐτοῦ. ἀγαλλιασώμεθα καὶ εὐφρανθῶμεν ἐν σοί· ἀγαπήσομεν μαστούς σου ὑπὲρ οἶνον· εὐθύτης ἠγάπησέν σε.
vulg: nigra sum sed formonsa filiae Hierusalem sicut tabernacula Cedar sicut pelles Salomonis
clem: Sponsa Nigra sum, sed formosa, fili Jerusalem, sicut tabernacula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomonis.
kjv: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: Μέλαινά εἰμι καὶ καλή, θυγατέρες Ἰσραήλ, ὡς σκηνώματα Κηδάρ, ὡς δέρρις Σαλωμών.
vulg: nolite me considerare quod fusca sim quia decoloravit me sol filii matris meae pugnaverunt contra me posuerunt me custodem in vineis vineam meam non custodivi
clem: Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim, quia decoloravit me sol. Filii matris me pugnaverunt contra me; posuerunt me custodem in vineis: vineam meam non custodivi.
kjv: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: μὴ βλέψητέ με, ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι μεμελανωμένη, ὅτι παρέβλεψέν με ὁ ἥλιος· υἱοὶ μητρός μου ἐμαχέσαντο ἐν ἐμοί, ἔθεντό με φυλάκισσαν ἐν ἀμπελῶσιν· ἀμπελῶνα ἐμὸν οὐκ ἐφύλαξα.
vulg: indica mihi quem diligit anima mea ubi pascas ubi cubes in meridie ne vagari incipiam per greges sodalium tuorum
clem: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie, ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum.
kjv: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: ἀπάγγειλόν μοι, ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου. ποῦ ποιμαίνεις, ποῦ κοιτάζεις ἐν μεσημβρίᾳ, μή ποτε γένωμαι ὡς περιβαλλομένη ἐπʼ ἀγέλας ἑταίρων σου.
vulg: si ignoras te o pulchra inter mulieres egredere et abi post vestigia gregum et pasce hedos tuos iuxta tabernacula pastorum
clem: Sponsus Si ignoras te, o pulcherrima inter mulieres, egredere, et abi post vestigia gregum, et pasce hdos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum.
kjv: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: Ἐὰν μὴ γνῷς σεαυτήν, ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιξίν, ἔξελθε οὺ ἐν πτέρναις τῶν ποιμνίων, καὶ ποίμαινε τὰς ἐρίφους σου ἐπὶ σκηνώμασιν τῶν ποιμένων.
vulg: equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis adsimilavi te amica mea
clem: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea.
kjv: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: Τῇ ἵππῳ μου ἐν ἅρμασιν Φαραὼ ὡμοἰωσά σε, ἡ πλησίον μου.
vulg: pulchrae sunt genae tuae sicut turturis collum tuum sicut monilia
clem: Pulchr sunt gen tu sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia.
kjv: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: τί ὡραιώθησαν σιαγόνες σου ὡς τρυγόνες, τράχηλός σου ὡς ὁρμίσκοις
vulg: murenulas aureas faciemus tibi vermiculatas argento
clem: Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento.
kjv: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: ὁμοιώματα χρυσίου ποιήσομέν σοι μετὰ στιγμάτων τοῦ ἀργυρίου.
vulg: dum esset rex in accubitu suo nardus mea dedit odorem suum
clem: Sponsa Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum.
kjv: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: Ἕως οὗ ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐν ἀνακλίσει αὐτοῦ, νάρδος μου ἔδωκεν ὀσμὴν αὐτοῦ.
vulg: fasciculus murrae dilectus meus mihi inter ubera mea commorabitur
clem: Fasciculus myrrh dilectus meus mihi; inter ubera mea commorabitur.
kjv: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: ἀπόδεσμος τῆς στακτῆς ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοί.
vulg: botrus cypri dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi
clem: Botrus cypri dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi.
kjv: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
lxx: ἐν ἀμπελῶσιν Ἐνγαδδεί.
vulg: ecce tu pulchra es amica mea ecce tu pulchra oculi tui columbarum
clem: Sponsus Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea! ecce tu pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum.
kjv: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.

wlc: אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
lxx: Ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή, ἡ πλησίν μου. ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή· ὀφθαλμοί σου περιστεραί.
vulg: ecce tu pulcher es dilecte mi et decorus lectulus noster floridus
clem: Sponsa Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus! Lectulus noster floridus.
kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.

wlc: דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
lxx: Ἰδοὺ εἶ καλός. ἀδελφιδός μου. καί γε ὡραῖος· πρὸς κλίνῃ ἡμῶν σύσκιος.
vulg: tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina laquearia nostra cypressina
clem: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina.]
kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.

wlc: עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
lxx: δοκοὶ σἴκων ἡμῶν κέδροι, φατνώματα ἡμῶν κυπάρισσοι.
kjv: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.

wlc: אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: ἐγὼ ἄνθος τοῦ πεδίου, κρίνον τῶν κοιλάδων.
vulg: ego flos campi et lilium convallium
clem: [Ego flos campi, et lilium convallium.
kjv: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: Ὡς κρίνον ἐν μέσῳ ἀκανθῶν, οὕτως ἡ πλησίον μου ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν θυγατέρων.
vulg: sicut lilium inter spinas sic amica mea inter filias
clem: Sponsus Sicut lilium inter spinas, sic amica mea inter filias.
kjv: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: Ὡς μῆλον ἐν τοῖς ξύλοις τοῦ δρυμοῦ, οὕτως ἀδελφιδός μου ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν υἱῶν· ἐν τῇ σκιᾷ αὐτοῦ ἐπεθύμησα καὶ ἐκάθισα, καὶ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ γλυκὺς ἐν λάρυγγί μου.
vulg: sicut malum inter ligna silvarum sic dilectus meus inter filios sub umbra illius quam desideraveram sedi et fructus eius dulcis gutturi meo
clem: Sponsa Sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, sic dilectus meus inter filios. Sub umbra illius quem desideraveram sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.
kjv: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: εἰσαγάγετέ με εἰς οἶκον τοῦ οἴνου, τάξατε ἐπʼ ἐμέ ἀγάπην.
vulg: introduxit me in cellam vinariam ordinavit in me caritatem
clem: Introduxit me in cellam vinariam; ordinavit in me caritatem.
kjv: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: στηρίσατέ με ἐν μύροις, στοιβάσατέ με ἐν μήλοις, ὅτι τετρωμένη ἀγάπης ἐγώ.
vulg: fulcite me floribus stipate me malis quia amore langueo
clem: Fulcite in me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo.
kjv: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: εὐώνυμος αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ τὴν κεφαλήν μου, καὶ ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ περιλήμψεταί με.
vulg: leva eius sub capite meo et dextera illius amplexabitur me
clem: Lva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.
kjv: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: Ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς, θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐν δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ, ἐὰν ἐγείρητε καὶ ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως οὗ θελήσῃ.
vulg: adiuro vos filiae Hierusalem per capreas cervosque camporum ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam quoadusque ipsa velit
clem: Sponsus Adjuro vos, fili Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit.
kjv: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: Φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου· ἰδοὺ οὗτος ἥκει πηδῶν ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη, διαλλόμενος ἐπὶ τοὺς βουνούς.
vulg: vox dilecti mei ecce iste venit saliens in montibus transiliens colles
clem: Sponsa Vox dilecti mei; ecce iste venit, saliens in montibus, transiliens colles.
kjv: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀδελφιδός μου τῇ δορκάδι ἢ νεβρῷ ἐλάφων ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη Βαιθήλ. ἰδοὺ οὗτος ὀπίσω τοῦ τοίχου ἡμῶν, παρακύπτων διὰ τῶν θυρίδων ἐκκύπτων διὰ τῶν δικτύων.
vulg: similis est dilectus meus capreae hinuloque cervorum en ipse stat post parietem nostrum despiciens per fenestras prospiciens per cancellos
clem: Similis est dilectus meus capre, hinnuloque cervorum. En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, respiciens per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos.
kjv: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: ἀποκρίνεται ἀδελφιδός μου καὶ λέγει μοι Ἀνάστα ἐλθέ, ἡ πλησίον μου, καλή μου, περιστερά μου.
vulg: et dilectus meus loquitur mihi surge propera amica mea formonsa mea et veni
clem: En dilectus meus loquitur mihi. Sponsus Surge, propera, amica mea, columba mea, formosa mea, et veni:
kjv: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ὁ χειμὼν παρῆλθεν, ὁ ὑετὸς ἀπῆλθεν, ἐπορεύθη ἑαυτῷ·
vulg: iam enim hiemps transiit imber abiit et recessit
clem: jam enim hiems transiit; imber abiit, et recessit.
kjv: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: τὰ ἄνθη ὤφθη ἐν τῇ γῇ, καιρὸς τῆς τομῆς ἔφθακεν, φωνὴ τοῦ τρυγόνος ἠκούσθη ἐν τῇ γῇ ἡμῶν·
vulg: flores apparuerunt in terra tempus putationis advenit vox turturis audita est in terra nostra
clem: Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra; tempus putationis advenit: vox turturis audita est in terra nostra;
kjv: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: ἡ συκῆ ἐξήνεγκεν ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς, αἱ ἄμπελοι κυπρίζουσιν, ἔδωκαν ὀσμήν. ἀνάστα ἐλθέ, ἡ πλησίον μου, καλή μου, περιστερά μου. καὶ ἐλθέ,
vulg: ficus protulit grossos suos vineae florent dederunt odorem surge amica mea speciosa mea et veni
clem: ficus protulit grossos suos; vine florentes dederunt odorem suum. Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni:
kjv: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
lxx: σὺ περιστερά μου, ἐν σκέπῃ τῆς πέτρας, ἐχόμενα τοῦ προτειχίσματος δεῖξόν μοι τὴν ὄψιν σου, καὶ ἀκούτισόν με τὴν φωνήν σου, ὅτι ἡ φωνή σου ἡδεῖα, καὶ ἡ ὄψις σου ὡραία.
vulg: columba mea in foraminibus petrae in caverna maceriae ostende mihi faciem tuam sonet vox tua in auribus meis vox enim tua dulcis et facies tua decora
clem: columba mea, in foraminibus petr, in caverna maceri, ostende mihi faciem tuam, sonet vox tua in auribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora.
kjv: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

wlc: אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
lxx: πιάσατε ἡμῖν ἀλώπεκας μικροὺς ἀφανίζοντας ἀμπελῶνας· καὶ αἱ ἄμπελοι ἡμῶν κυπρίζουσαι.
vulg: capite nobis vulpes vulpes parvulas quae demoliuntur vineas nam vinea nostra floruit
clem: Sponsa Capite nobis vulpes parvulas qu demoliuntur vineas: nam vinea nostra floruit.
kjv: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

wlc: דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
lxx: βελφιδός μου ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ αὐτῷ· ὁ ποιμαίνων ἐν τοῖς κρίνοις,
vulg: dilectus meus mihi et ego illi qui pascitur inter lilia
clem: Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi, qui pascitur inter lilia,
kjv: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

wlc: עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
lxx: ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ κινηθῶσιν αἱ σκιαί. ἀπόστρεψον, ὁμοιώθητι σύ, ἀδελφιδέ, τῷ δόρκωνι ἢ νεβρῷ ἐλάφων ἐπὶ ὄρη κοιλωμάτων.
vulg: donec adspiret dies et inclinentur umbrae revertere similis esto dilecte mi capreae aut hinulo cervorum super montes Bether
clem: donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbr. Revertere; similis esto, dilecte mi, capre, hinnuloque cervorum super montes Bether.]
kjv: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

wlc: אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: ἐπὶ κοίτην μου ἐν νυξὶν ἐζήτησα ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτόν, ἐκάλεσα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουσέν μου.
vulg: in lectulo meo per noctes quaesivi quem diligit anima mea quaesivi illum et non inveni
clem: [In lectulo meo, per noctes, qusivi quem diligit anima mea: qusivi illum, et non inveni.
kjv: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: ἀναστήσομαι δὴ καὶ κυκλώσω ἐν τῇ πόλει, ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις, καὶ ζητήσω ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτόν.
vulg: surgam et circuibo civitatem per vicos et plateas quaeram quem diligit anima mea quaesivi illum et non inveni
clem: Surgam, et circuibo civitatem: per vicos et plateas quram quem diligit anima mea: qusivi illum, et non inveni.
kjv: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: εὕροσάν με οἱ τηροῦντες, οἱ κυκλοῦντες ἐν τῇ πόλει Μὴ ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου εἴδετε;
vulg: invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem num quem dilexit anima mea vidistis
clem: Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem: Num quem diligit anima mea vidistis?
kjv: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: ὡς μικρὸν ὅτε παρῆλθον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, ἕως οὗ εὗρον ὃν ἠγάπησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· ἐκράτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκα αὐτόν, ἕως οὗ εἰσήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον μητρός μου καὶ εἰς ταμεῖον τῆς συλλαβούσης με.
vulg: paululum cum pertransissem eos inveni quem diligit anima mea tenui eum nec dimittam donec introducam illum in domum matris meae et in cubiculum genetricis meae
clem: Paululum cum pertransissem eos, inveni quem diligit anima mea: tenui eum, nec dimittam, donec introducam illum in domum matris me, et in cubiculum genetricis me.
kjv: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: Ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς, θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ, ἐὰν ἐγείρητε καὶ ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως ἂν θελήσῃ.
vulg: adiuro vos filiae Hierusalem per capreas cervosque camporum ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam donec ipsa velit
clem: Sponsus Adjuro vos, fili Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.
kjv: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: Τίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα ἀπὸ τῆς ἐρήμου. ὡς στελέχη καπνοῦ τεθυμιαμένη σμύρναν καὶ λίβανον ἀπὸ πάντων κονιορτῶν μυρεψοῦ;
vulg: quae est ista quae ascendit per desertum sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus murrae et turis et universi pulveris pigmentarii
clem: Chorus Qu est ista qu ascendit per desertum sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrh, et thuris, et universi pulveris pigmentarii?
kjv: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: ἰδοὺ ἡ κλίνη τοῦ Σαλωμών, ἐξήκοντα δυνατοὶ κύκλῳ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ δυνατῶν Ἰσραήλ·
vulg: en lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israhel
clem: En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Isral,
kjv: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: πάντες κατέχοντες ῥομφαίαν, δεδιδαγμένοι πόλεμον· ἀνὴρ ῥομφαία αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ μηρὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ θάμβους ἐν νυξίν.
vulg: omnes tenentes gladios et ad bella doctissimi uniuscuiusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos
clem: omnes tenentes gladios, et ad bella doctissimi: uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos.
kjv: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: φορεῖον ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ ὁ βασιλεὺς Σαλωμὼν ἀπὸ ξύλων τοῦ Λιβάνου·
vulg: ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani
clem: Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani;
kjv: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: στύλους αὐτοῦ ἐποίησεν ἀργύριον, καὶ ἀνάκλιτον αὐτοῦ χρύσεον· ἐπίβασις αὐτοῦ πορφυρᾶ, ἐντὸς αὐτοῦ λιθόστρωτον, ἀγάπην ἀπὸ θυγατέρων Ἰερουσαλήμ.
vulg: columnas eius fecit argenteas reclinatorium aureum ascensum purpureum media caritate constravit propter filias Hierusalem
clem: columnas ejus fecit argenteas, reclinatorium aureum, ascensum purpureum; media caritate constravit, propter filias Jerusalem.
kjv: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: ἐξέλθατε καὶ ἴδετε ἐν τῷ βασιλεῖ Σαλωμών, ἐν τῷ στεφάνῳ ᾧ ἐστεφάνωσεν αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ νυμφεύσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐφροσύνης καρδίας αὐτοῦ.
vulg: egredimini et videte filiae Sion regem Salomonem in diademate quo coronavit eum mater sua in die disponsionis illius et in die laetitiae cordis eius
clem: Egredimini et videte, fili Sion, regem Salomonem in diademate quo coronavit illum mater sua in die desponsationis illius, et in die ltiti cordis ejus.]
kjv: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: Ἰδοὺ εἶ καλὴ πλησίον μου, ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή. ὀφθαλμοί σου περιστεραὶ ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεώς σου. τρίχαμά σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν αἰγῶν αἳ ἀπεκαλύφθησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Γαλαάδ.
vulg: quam pulchra es amica mea quam pulchra es oculi tui columbarum absque eo quod intrinsecus latet capilli tui sicut greges caprarum quae ascenderunt de monte Galaad
clem: [ Sponsus Quam pulchra es, amica mea! quam pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet. Capilli tui sicut greges caprarum qu ascenderunt de monte Galaad.
kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: ὀδόντες σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν κεκαρμέναων αἳ ἀνέβησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ λουτροῦ, αἱ πᾶσαι διδυμεύουσαι, καὶ ἀτεκνοῦσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐταῖς.
vulg: dentes tui sicut greges tonsarum quae ascenderunt de lavacro omnes gemellis fetibus et sterilis non est inter eas
clem: Dentes tui sicut greges tonsarum qu ascenderunt de lavacro; omnes gemellis ftibus, et sterilis non est inter eas.
kjv: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: ὡς σπαρτίον τὸ κόκκινον χείλη σου, καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὡραία· ὡς λέπυρον ῥόας μῆλόν σου ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεως σου.
vulg: sicut vitta coccinea labia tua et eloquium tuum dulce sicut fragmen mali punici ita genae tuae absque eo quod intrinsecus latet
clem: Sicut vitta coccinea labia tua, et eloquium tuum dulce. Sicut fragmen mali punici, ita gen tu, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet.
kjv: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: ὡς πύργος Δαυεὶδ τράχηλός σου, ὁ ᾠκοδομημένος εἰς Θαλπιώθ. χίλιοι θυρεοὶ κρέμανται ἐπʼ αὐτόν, πᾶσαι βολίδες τῶν δυνατῶν.
vulg: sicut turris David collum tuum quae aedificata est cum propugnaculis mille clypei pendent ex ea omnis armatura fortium
clem: Sicut turris David collum tuum, qu dificata est cum propugnaculis; mille clypei pendant ex ea, omnis armatura fortium.
kjv: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: δύο μαστοί σου ὡς δύο νεβροὶ δἰδυμοι δορκάδος οἱ νεμόμενοι ἐν κρίνοις.
vulg: duo ubera tua sicut duo hinuli capreae gemelli qui pascuntur in liliis
clem: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, capre gemelli, qui pascuntur in liliis.
kjv: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα καὶ κινηθῶσιν αἱ σκιαί, πορεύσομαι ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τῆς σμύρνης καὶ πρὸς τὸν βουνὸν τοῦ Λιβάνου.
vulg: donec adspiret dies et inclinentur umbrae vadam ad montem murrae et ad collem turis
clem: Donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbr, vadam ad montem myrrh, et ad collem thuris.
kjv: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: ὅλη καλὴ εἶ πλησίον μου, καὶ μῶμος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν σοί. δεῦρο ἀπὸ Λιβάνου, νύμφη, δεῦρο ἀπὸ Λιβάνου· ἐλεύσῃ καὶ διελεύσῃ ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς πίστεως. ἀπὸ κεφαλῆς Σανεὶρ καὶ Ἑρμών, ἀπὸ μανδρῶν λεόντων, ἀπὸ ὀρέων παρδάλεων.
vulg: tota pulchra es amica mea et macula non est in te
clem: Tota pulchra es, amica mea, et macula non est in te.
kjv: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
vulg: veni de Libano sponsa veni de Libano veni coronaberis de capite Amana de vertice Sanir et Hermon de cubilibus leonum de montibus pardorum
clem: Veni de Libano, sponsa mea: veni de Libano, veni, coronaberis: de capite Amana, de vertice Sanir et Hermon, de cubilibus leonum, de montibus pardorum.
kjv: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: ἐκαρδίωσας ἡμᾶς, ἀδελφή μου νύμφη· ἐκαρδίωσας ἡμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου, ἐν μιᾷ, ἐν θέματι τραχήλων σου.
vulg: vulnerasti cor meum soror mea sponsa vulnerasti cor meum in uno oculorum tuorum et in uno crine colli tui
clem: Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa; vulnerasti cor meum in uno oculorum tuorum, et in uno crine colli tui.
kjv: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: τί ἐκαλλιώθησαν μαστοί σου ἀπὸ οἴνου, καὶ ὀσμὴ ἱματίων σου ὑπὲρ πάντα ἀρώματα
vulg: quam pulchrae sunt mammae tuae soror mea sponsa pulchriora ubera tua vino et odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata
clem: Quam pulchr sunt mamm tu, soror mea sponsa! pulchriora sunt ubera tua vino, et odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata.
kjv: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: κηρίον ἀποστάζουσιν χείλη σου, νύμφη· μέλι καὶ γάλα ὑπὸ τὴν γλῶσσάν σου, καὶ ὀσμὴ ἱματίων σου ὡς ὀσμὴ Λβάνου.
vulg: favus distillans labia tua sponsa mel et lac sub lingua tua et odor vestimentorum tuorum sicut odor turis
clem: Favus distillans labia tua, sponsa; mel et lac sub lingua tua: et odor vestimentorum tuorum sicut odor thuris.
kjv: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: κῆπος κεκλεισμένος ἀδελφή μου νύμφη, κῆπος κεκλεισμένος, πηγὴ ἐσφραγισμένη·
vulg: hortus conclusus soror mea sponsa hortus conclusus fons signatus
clem: Hortus conclusus soror mea, sponsa, hortus conclusus, fons signatus.
kjv: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: ἀποστολαί σου παράδεισος μετὰ καρποῦ ἀκροδρύων, κύπροι μετὰ νάρδων·
vulg: emissiones tuae paradisus malorum punicorum cum pomorum fructibus cypri cum nardo
clem: Emissiones tu paradisus malorum punicorum, cum pomorum fructibus, cypri cum nardo.
kjv: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
lxx: νάρδος καὶ κρόκος, κάλαμος καὶ κιννάμαωμον μετὰ πάντων ξύλων τοῦ Λιβάνου, σμύρνα ἀλὼθ μετὰ πάνταον πρώτων μύρων·
vulg: nardus et crocus fistula et cinnamomum cum universis lignis Libani murra et aloe cum omnibus primis unguentis
clem: Nardus et crocus, fistula et cinnamomum, cum universis lignis Libani; myrrha et alo, cum omnibus primis unguentis.
kjv: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

wlc: אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
lxx: πηγὴ κήπου καὶ φρέαρ ὕδατος ζῶντος καὶ ῥοιζοῦντος ἀπὸ τοῦ Λιβάνου.
vulg: fons hortorum puteus aquarum viventium quae fluunt impetu de Libano
clem: Fons hortorum, puteus aquarum viventium, qu fluunt impetu de Libano.
kjv: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

wlc: דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
lxx: Ἐξεγέρθητι, βορρᾶ· καὶ ἔρχου. νότε, καὶ διάπνευσον κῆπόν μου, καὶ ῥευσάτωσαν ἀρώματά μου.
vulg: surge aquilo et veni auster perfla hortum meum et fluant aromata illius
clem: Sponsa Surge, aquilo, et veni, auster: perfla hortum meum, et fluant aromata illius.]
kjv: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

wlc: עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: καταβήτω ἀδελφιδός μου εἰς κῆπον αὐτοῦ καὶ φαγέτω καρπὸν ἀκροδρύων αὐτοῦ. (¹)Εἰοῆλθον εἰς κῆπον, ἀδελφή μου νύμφη· ἐτρύγησα σμύρναν μου μετὰ ἀρωμάτων μου, ἔφαγον ἄρτον μου μετὰ μέλιτός μου, ἔπιον οἶνόν μου μετὰ γάλακτός μου. φάγετε, πλησίοι, καὶ πίετε καὶ μεθύσθητε, ἀδελφοί
vulg: veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum et comedat fructum pomorum suorum veni in hortum meum soror mea sponsa messui murram meam cum aromatibus meis comedi favum cum melle meo bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo comedite amici bibite et inebriamini carissimi
clem: [Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, et comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Sponsus Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa; messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis; comedi favum cum melle meo; bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo; comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi.
kjv: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: Ἐγὼ καθεύδω, καὶ ἡ καρδία μου ἀγρυπνεῖ φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου, κρούει ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν Ἄνοιξόν μοι, ἀδελφή μου, ἡ πλησίον μου. περιστερά μου, τελεία μου, ὅτι ἡ κεφαλή μου ἐπλήσθη δρόσου καὶ οἱ βόστρυχοί μου ψεκάδων νυκτός.
vulg: ego dormio et cor meum vigilat vox dilecti mei pulsantis aperi mihi soror mea amica mea columba mea inmaculata mea quia caput meum plenum est rore et cincinni mei guttis noctium
clem: Sponsa Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat. Vox dilecti mei pulsantis: Sponsus Aperi mihi, soror mea, amica mea, columba mea, immaculata mea, quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium.
kjv: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: ἐξεδυσάμην τὸν χιτῶνά μου, πῶς ἐνδύσωμαι αὐτόν; ἐνιψάμην τοὺς πόδας μου, πῶς μολυνῶ αὐτούς;
vulg: expoliavi me tunica mea quomodo induar illa lavi pedes meos quomodo inquinabo illos
clem: Sponsa Expoliavi me tunica mea: quomodo induar illa? lavi pedes meos: quomodo inquinabo illos?
kjv: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: ἀδελφιδός μου ἀπέστειλεν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀπῆς. καὶ ἡ κοιλία μου ἐθροήθη ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
vulg: dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen et venter meus intremuit ad tactum eius
clem: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus.
kjv: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: ἀνέστην ἐγὼ ἀνοῖξαι τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου. χεῖρές μου ἔσταξαν σμύρναν, δάκτυλοί μου σμύρναν πλήρη ἐπὶ χεῖρας τοῦ κλείθρου.
vulg: surrexi ut aperirem dilecto meo manus meae stillaverunt murra digiti mei pleni murra probatissima
clem: Surrexi ut aperirem dilecto meo; manus me stillaverunt myrrham, et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima.
kjv: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: ἤνοιξα ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου, ἀδελφιδός μου παρῆλθεν· ψυχή μου ἐξῆλθεν ἐν λόγῳ αὐτοῦ· ἐζήτησα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ εὖρον αὐτόν, ἐκάλεσα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουσέν μου.
vulg: pessulum ostii aperui dilecto meo at ille declinaverat atque transierat anima mea liquefacta est ut locutus est quaesivi et non inveni illum vocavi et non respondit mihi
clem: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo, at ille declinaverat, atque transierat. Anima mea liquefacta est, ut locutus est; qusivi, et non inveni illum; vocavi, et non respondit mihi.
kjv: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: εὕροσάν με οἱ φύλακες οἱ κυκλοῦντες ἐν τῇ πόλει. ἐπάταξάν με, ἐτραυμάτισάν με· ἦραν τὸ θέριστρόν μου ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ φύλακες τῶν τειχέων
vulg: invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem percusserunt me vulneraverunt me tulerunt pallium meum mihi custodes murorum
clem: Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem; percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me. Tulerunt pallium meum mihi custodes murorum.
kjv: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: Ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς, θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ, ἐὰν εὕρητε τὸν ἀδελφιδόν μου, τί ἀπαγγείλητε αὐτῷ; ὅτι τετρωμένη ἀγάπης ἐγώ.
vulg: adiuro vos filiae Hierusalem si inveneritis dilectum meum ut nuntietis ei quia amore langueo
clem: Adjuro vos, fili Jerusalem, si inveneritis dilectum meum, ut nuntietis ei quia amore langueo.
kjv: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: Τί ἀδελφιδός σου ἀπὸ ἀδελφιδοῦ, ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιείν, τἰ ἀδελφιδός σου ἀπὸ ἀδελφιδοῦ, ὅτι οὕτως ὥρκισας ἡμᾶς;
vulg: qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto o pulcherrima mulierum qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto quia sic adiurasti nos
clem: Chorus Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum? qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, quia sic adjurasti nos?
kjv: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: Ἀδελφιδός μου λευκὸς καὶ πυρρός, ἐκλελοχισμένος ἀπὸ μυριάδων.
vulg: dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus electus ex milibus
clem: Sponsa Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus; electus ex millibus.
kjv: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ χρυσίον καὶ φάζ, βόστρυχοι αὐτοῦ ἐλάται, μέλανες ὡς κόραξ.
vulg: caput eius aurum optimum comae eius sicut elatae palmarum nigrae quasi corvus
clem: Caput ejus aurum optimum; com ejus sicut elat palmarum, nigr quasi corvus.
kjv: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: Ζφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς περιστεραὶ ἐπὶ πληρώματα ὑδάτων λελουσμέναι ἐν γάλακτι, καθήμεναι ἐπὶ πληρώματα.
vulg: oculi eius sicut columbae super rivulos aquarum quae lacte sunt lotae et resident iuxta fluenta plenissima
clem: Oculi ejus sicut columb super rivulos aquarum, qu lacte sunt lot, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima.
kjv: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: σιαγόνες αὐτοῦ ὡς φιάλαι τοῦ ἀρώματος φύουσαι μυρεψικά, χείλη αὐτοῦ κρίνα στάζοντα σμύρναν πλήρη.
vulg: genae illius sicut areolae aromatum consitae a pigmentariis labia eius lilia distillantia murram primam
clem: Gen illius sicut areol aromatum, consit a pigmentariis. Labia ejus lilia, distillantia myrrham primam.
kjv: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
lxx: χεῖρες αὐτοῦ τορευταὶ χρυσαῖ πεπληραομέναι Θαρσείς. κοιλία αὐτοῦ πυξίον ἐλεφάντινον ἐπὶ λίθου σαπφείρου.
vulg: manus illius tornatiles aureae plenae hyacinthis venter eius eburneus distinctus sapphyris
clem: Manus illius tornatiles, aure, plen hyacinthis. Venter ejus eburneus, distinctus sapphiris.
kjv: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

wlc: אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
lxx: κνῆμαι αὐτοῦ στύλοι μαρμάρινοι τεθεμελιωμένοι ἐπὶ βάσεις χρυσᾶς· εἶδος αὐτοῦ ὡς Λίβανος, ἐκλεκτὸς ὡς κέδροι.
vulg: crura illius columnae marmoreae quae fundatae sunt super bases aureas species eius ut Libani electus ut cedri
clem: Crura illius column marmore qu fundat sunt super bases aureas. Species ejus ut Libani, electus ut cedri.
kjv: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

wlc: דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
lxx: φάρυγξ αὐτοῦ γλυκασμοὶ καὶ ὅλος ἐπιθυμία. οὗτος ἀδελφιδός μου καὶ οὗτος πλησίον μου, θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ.
vulg: guttur illius suavissimum et totus desiderabilis talis est dilectus meus et iste est amicus meus filiae Hierusalem
clem: Guttur illius suavissimum, et totus desiderabilis. Talis est dilectus meus, et ipse est amicus meus, fili Jerusalem.
kjv: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

wlc: עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
lxx: Ποῦ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἀδελφιδός σου, ἡ καλὴ ἐν γυναιξίνς; ποῦ ἀπέβλεψεν ὁ ἀδελφιδός σους; καὶ ζητήσομεν αὐτὸν μετὰ σοῦ.
vulg: quo abiit dilectus tuus o pulcherrima mulierum quo declinavit dilectus tuus et quaeremus eum tecum
clem: Chorus Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum? quo declinavit dilectus tuus? et quremus eum tecum.]

wlc: אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: Ἀδελφός μου κατέβη εἰς κῆπον αὐτοῦ εἰς φιάλας τοῦ ἀρῶματος, ποιμαίνειν ἐν κήποις καὶ συλλέγειν κρίνα.
vulg: dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum ad areolam aromatis ut pascatur in hortis et lilia colligat
clem: [ Sponsa Dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum ad areolam aromatum, ut pascatur in hortis, et lilia colligat.
kjv: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: ἐγκ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου καὶ ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοί, ὁ ποιμαίνων ἐν τοῖς κρίνοις.
vulg: ego dilecto meo et dilectus meus mihi qui pascitur inter lilia
clem: Ego dilecto meo, et dilectus meus mihi, qui pascitur inter lilia.
kjv: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: Καλὴ εἶ πλησίον μου, ὡς εὐδοκία, ὡραία ὡς Ἰερουσαλὴμ, θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναι.
vulg: pulchra es amica mea suavis et decora sicut Hierusalem terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata
clem: Sponsus Pulchra es, amica mea; suavis, et decora sicut Jerusalem; terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata.
kjv: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: ἀπόστρεψον ὀφθαλμούς σου ἀπεναντίον μου, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἀνεπτέραοσαν με. τρίχωμά σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν αἰγῶν αἳ ἀνεφάνησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Γαλαὰδ,
vulg: averte oculos tuos a me quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt capilli tui sicut grex caprarum quae apparuerunt de Galaad
clem: Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt. Capilli tui sicut grex caprarum qu apparuerunt de Galaad.
kjv: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: ὀδόντες σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν κεκαρμένων αἳ ἀνέβησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ λουτροῦ, αἱ πᾶσαι διδυμεύουσαι, καὶ ἀτεκνοῦσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐταῖς. ὡς σπαρτίον τὸ κόκκινον χείλη σου, καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὡραία.
vulg: dentes tui sicut grex ovium quae ascenderunt de lavacro omnes gemellis fetibus et sterilis non est in eis
clem: Dentes tui sicut grex ovium qu ascenderunt de lavacro: omnes gemellis ftibus, et sterilis non est in eis.
kjv: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: ὡς λέπυρον ῥόας μῆλόν σου ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεως σου.
vulg: sicut cortex mali punici genae tuae absque occultis tuis
clem: Sicut cortex mali punici, sic gen tu, absque occultis tuis.
kjv: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: ἐξήκοντά εἰσιν βασίύισσαι, καὶ ὀγδοήκοντα παλλακαί, καὶ νεάνιδες ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός·
vulg: sexaginta sunt reginae et octoginta concubinae et adulescentularum non est numerus
clem: Sexaginta sunt regin, et octoginta concubin, et adolescentularum non est numerus.
kjv: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: μία ἐστὶν περιστερά μου, τελεία μου, μία ἐστὶν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς, ἐκλεκτή ἐστιν τῇ τεκούσῃ αὐτῆς. εἴδοσαν αὐτὴν θυγατέρες καὶ ναεαοωῦσιν αὐτήν, βασίλισσαι καί γε παλλακαί, καὶ αἰνέσουσιν αὐτήν.
vulg: una est columba mea perfecta mea una est matris suae electa genetrici suae viderunt illam filiae et beatissimam praedicaverunt reginae et concubinae et laudaverunt eam
clem: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matris su, electa genetrici su. Viderunt eam fili, et beatissimam prdicaverunt; regin et concubin, et laudaverunt eam.
kjv: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: Τίς αὕτη ἡ ἐκκύπτουσα ὡσεὶ ὄρθρος. καλὴ ὡς σελήνη, ἐκλεκτὴ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναις
vulg: quae est ista quae progreditur quasi aurora consurgens pulchra ut luna electa ut sol terribilis ut acies ordinata
clem: Qu est ista qu progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna, electa ut sol, terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata?
kjv: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: Εἰς κῆπον καρύας κατέβην ἰδεῖν ἐν γενήμασιν τοῦ χειμάρρου, ἰδεῖν εἰ ἤνθησεν ἡ ἄμπελος, ἐξήνθησαν αἱ ῥόαι· ἐκεῖ δώσω τοὺς μαστούς μου σοί.
vulg: descendi ad hortum nucum ut viderem poma convallis ut inspicerem si floruisset vinea et germinassent mala punica
clem: Sponsa Descendi in hortum nucum, ut viderem poma convallium, et inspicerem si floruisset vinea, et germinassent mala punica.
kjv: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: οὐκ ἔγνω ἡ ψυχή μου· ἔθετό με ἄρματα Ἀμειναδάβ.
vulg: nescivi anima mea conturbavit me propter quadrigas Aminadab
clem: Nescivi: anima mea conturbavit me, propter quadrigas Aminadab.
kjv: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: Ἐπίστρεφε, ἐπίστρεφε, ἡ Σουμανεῖτις·
vulg: revertere revertere Sulamitis revertere revertere ut intueamur te
clem: Chorus Revertere, revertere, Sulamitis! revertere, revertere ut intueamur te.]
kjv: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
kjv: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: Τί δψεοθε ἐν τῆ Σουμανείτιδις ἡ ἐρχομένη ὡς χοροὶ τῶν παρεμβολῶν. (2) Ὡραιώθησαν διαβήματά σου ἐν ὑποδήμασιν, θύγατερ Ναδάβ. ὀυθμοὶ μηρῶν σου ὃμοιοι ὁρμίσκοις. ἔργον τεχνίτου.
vulg: quid videbis in Sulamiten nisi choros castrorum quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calciamentis filia principis iunctura feminum tuorum sicut monilia quae fabricata sunt manu artificis
clem: [ Sponsa Quid videbis in Sulamite, nisi choros castrorum? Chorus Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis, filia principis! Junctur femorum tuorum sicut monilia qu fabricata sunt manu artificis.
kjv: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: ὀμφαλός σου κρατὴρ τορευτός, μὴ ὑστερούμενος κρᾶμα· κοιλία σου θιμωνιὰ σίτου πεφραγμένη ἐν κρίνοις.
vulg: umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis numquam indigens poculis venter tuus sicut acervus tritici vallatus liliis
clem: Umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis, numquam indigens poculis. Venter tuus sicut acervus tritici vallatus liliis.
kjv: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: δύο μαστοί σου ὡς δύο νεβροὶ δίδυμοι δορκάδος·
vulg: duo ubera tua sicut duo hinuli gemelli capreae
clem: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, gemelli capre.
kjv: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: ὁ τράχηλός σου ὡς πύργος ἐλεφάντινος. οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ὡς λίμναι ἐν Ἐσεβῶν, ἐν πύλαις θυγατρὸς πολλῶν. μυκτήρ σου ὡς πύργος τοῦ Λιβάνου σκοπεύωυ πρόσαοπον Δαμασκοῦ.
vulg: collum tuum sicut turris eburnea oculi tui sicut piscinae in Esebon quae sunt in porta filiae multitudinis nasus tuus sicut turris Libani quae respicit contra Damascum
clem: Collum tuum sicut turris eburnea; oculi tui sicut piscin in Hesebon qu sunt in porta fili multitudinis. Nasus tuus sicut turris Libani, qu respicit contra Damascum.
kjv: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: κεφαλή σου ἐπὶ σέ ὡς Κάρμηλος, καὶ πλόκιον κεφαλῆς σου ὡς πορφύρα, βασύιεὺς δεδεμένος ἐν παραδρομαῖς.
vulg: caput tuum ut Carmelus et comae capitis tui sicut purpura regis vincta canalibus
clem: Caput tuum ut Carmelus; et com capitis tui sicut purpura regis vincta canalibus.
kjv: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: τί ὡραιώθης, καὶ τί ἡδύνθης, ἀγάπη, ἐν τρυφαῖς σους
vulg: quam pulchra es et quam decora carissima in deliciis
clem: Sponsus Quam pulchra es, et quam decora, carissima, in deliciis!
kjv: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: τοῦτο μέγεθός σου· ὡμοιώθης τῷ φοίνικι, καὶ οἱ μαστοί σου τοῖς βότρυσιν.
vulg: statura tua adsimilata est palmae et ubera tua botris
clem: Statura tua assimilata est palm, et ubera tua botris.
kjv: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: εἶπα Ἀναβήσομαι ἐπὶ τῷ φοίνικι, κρατήσω τῶυ ὕψεωυ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἔσονται δὴ μαστοί σου ὡς βότρυες τῆς ἀμπέλου, καὶ ὀσμὴ ῥινός σου ὡς μῆλα,
vulg: dixi ascendam in palmam adprehendam fructus eius et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vineae et odor oris tui sicut malorum
clem: Dixi: Ascendam in palmam, et apprehendam fructus ejus; et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vine, et odor oris tui sicut malorum.
kjv: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: καὶ ὁ λάρυγξ σου ὡς οἶνος ὁ ἀγαθός, πορευόμενος τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου εἰς εὐθύτητα, ἱκανούμενος χείλεσίν μου καὶ ὀδοῦσιν.
vulg: guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum dignum dilecto meo ad potandum labiisque et dentibus illius ruminandum
clem: Guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum, dignum dilecto meo ad potandum, labiisque et dentibus illius ad ruminandum.
kjv: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: Ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου. καὶ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ἡ ἐπιστροφὴ αὐτοῦ.
vulg: ego dilecto meo et ad me conversio eius
clem: Sponsa Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus.
kjv: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: ἐλθὲ, ἀδελφιδέ μου, ἐξέλθωμεν εἰς ἀγρόν. αὐλισθῶμευ ἐν κώμαις·
vulg: veni dilecte mi egrediamur in agrum commoremur in villis
clem: Veni, dilecte mi, egrediamur in agrum, commoremur in villis.
kjv: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: ἐπίστρεφε, ἐπίστρεφε, καὶ ὀψόμεθα ἐν σοί. ὀρθρίσωμεν εἰς ἀμπελῶνας, ἴδωμεν εἰ ἤνθησεν ἡ ἄμπελος, ἤνθησεν ὁ κυπρισμός, ἤνθησαν αἱ ῥὸαι· ἐκεῖ δώσω τοὺς μαστούς μου σοί.
vulg: mane surgamus ad vineas videamus si floruit vinea si flores fructus parturiunt si floruerunt mala punica ibi dabo tibi ubera mea
clem: Mane surgamus ad vineas: videamus si floruit vinea, si flores fructus parturiunt, si floruerunt mala punica; ibi dabo tibi ubera mea.
kjv: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: οἱ μανδραγόραι ἔδωκαν ὀσμήν, καὶ ἐπὶ θύραις ἡμῶν πάντα ἀκρόδρυα, νέα πρὸς παλαιά, ἀδελφιδέ μου, ἐτήρησά σοι.
vulg: mandragorae dederunt odorem in portis nostris omnia poma nova et vetera dilecte mi servavi tibi
clem: Mandragor dederunt odorem in portis nostris omnia poma: nova et vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi.]
kjv: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים ׃
lxx: τίς δῴη σε ἀδελφιδόν μου, θηλάζοντα μαστοὺς μητρός μους εὑροῦσά σε ἔξω φιλήσω σε, καί γε οὐκ ἐξουδενώσουσίν μοι.
vulg: quis mihi det te fratrem meum sugentem ubera matris meae ut inveniam te foris et deosculer et iam me nemo despiciat
clem: [Quis mihi det te fratrem meum, sugentem ubera matris me, ut inveniam te foris, et deosculer te, et jam me nemo despiciat?
kjv: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.

wlc: כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת ׃
lxx: παραλήμψομαί σε, εἰσάξω σε εἰς οἶκον μητρός μου καὶ εἰς ταμεῖον τῆς συλλαβούσης με· ποτιῶ σε ἀπὸ οἴνου τοῦ μυρεψικοῦ,
vulg: adprehendam te et ducam in domum matris meae ibi me docebis et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito et mustum malorum granatorum meorum
clem: Apprehendam te, et ducam in domum matris me: ibi me docebis, et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito, et mustum malorum granatorum meorum.
kjv: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

wlc: כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי ׃
lxx: εὐώνυμος αὐτοῦ ὑπὸ τὴν κεφαλὴν μου. ἀπὸ νάματος ῥοῶν σου. καὶ ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ περιλήμψεταί με.
vulg: leva eius sub capite meo et dextera illius amplexabitur me
clem: Lva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.
kjv: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

wlc: הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל־בֵּית הַיָּיִן וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה ׃
lxx: Ὥρκισα ὑμᾶς, θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐν ταῖς δυνάμεσιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἰσχύσεσιν τοῦ ἀγροῦ, ἐὰν ἐγείρητε καὶ ἐξεγείρητε τὴν ἀγάπην ἕως ἂυ θελήσῃ.
vulg: adiuro vos filiae Hierusalem ne suscitetis et evigilare faciatis dilectam donec ipsa velit
clem: Sponsus Adjuro vos, fili Jerusalem, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.
kjv: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.

wlc: סַמְּכוּנִי בָּאֲשִׁישׁוֹת רַפְּדוּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִים כִּי־חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה אָנִי ׃
lxx: Tίς αὕτη ἡ ἀναβαίνουσα λελευκαθισμένη. ἐπιστηριζομένη ἐπὶ τὸν ἀδελφιδὸν αὐτῆς; Ὑπὸ μῆλον ἐξήγειρά σε· ἐκεῖ ὠδίνησέν σε ἡ μήτηρ σου, ἐκεῖ ὠδίνησέν σε ἡ τεκοῦσά σου.
vulg: quae est ista quae ascendit de deserto deliciis affluens et nixa super dilectum suum sub arbore malo suscitavi te ibi corrupta est mater tua ibi violata est genetrix tua
clem: Chorus Qu est ista qu ascendit de deserto, deliciis affluens, innixa super dilectum suum? Sponsus Sub arbore malo suscitavi te; ibi corrupta est mater tua, ibi violata est genitrix tua.
kjv: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth that bare thee.

wlc: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי ׃
lxx: θές με ὡς σφραγῖδα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου, ὡς σφραγῖδα ἐπὶ τὸν βραχίονά σου· ὅτι κραταιὰ ὡς θάνατος ἀγάπη, σκληρὸς ὡς ᾂδης ζῆλος· περίπτερα αὐτῆς περίπτερα πυρός, φλόγες αὐτῆς·
vulg: pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum ut signaculum super brachium tuum quia fortis est ut mors dilectio dura sicut inferus aemulatio lampades eius lampades ignis atque flammarum
clem: Sponsa Pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum, ut signaculum super brachium tuum, quia fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut infernus mulatio: lampades ejus lampades ignis atque flammarum.
kjv: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.

wlc: הִשְׁבַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַםִ בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אִם־תָּעִירוּ וְאִם־תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת־הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּץ ׃ ס
lxx: ὕδωρ πολὺ οὐ δυνήσεται σβέσαι τὴυ ἀγάπην, καὶ ποταμοὶ οὐ συνκλύσουσιν αὐτήν. ἐὰν δῷ ἀνὴρ τὸν πάντα βίον αὐτοῦ ἐν τῆ ἀγάπῃ, ἐξουδενώσει ἐξουδενώσουσιν αὐτόν.
vulg: aquae multae non poterunt extinguere caritatem nec flumina obruent illam si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suae pro dilectione quasi nihil despicient eum
clem: Aqu mult non potuerunt extinguere caritatem, nec flumina obruent illam. Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus su pro dilectione, quasi nihil despiciet eam.
kjv: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

wlc: קוֹל דּוֹדִי הִנֵּה־זֶה בָּא מְדַלֵּג עַל־הֶהָרִים מְקַפֵּץ עַל־הַגְּבָעוֹת ׃
lxx: Ἀδελφὴ ἡμῖν μικρὰ καὶ μαστοὺς οὐκ ἔχει. τί ποιήσωμεν τῇ ἀδελφῇ ἡμῶν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ ἐὰν λαληθῇ ἐν αὐτῇ;
vulg: soror nostra parva et ubera non habet quid faciemus sorori nostrae in die quando adloquenda est
clem: Chorus Fratrum Soror nostra parva, et ubera non habet; quid faciemus sorori nostr in die quando alloquenda est?
kjv: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

wlc: דּוֹמֶה דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים הִנֵּה־זֶה עוֹמֵד אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן־הַחֲלֹּנוֹת מֵצִיץ מִן־הַחֲרַכִּים ׃
lxx: εἰ τεῖχός ἐστιν, οἰκοδομήσωμεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν ἐπάλξεις ἀργυρᾶς· καὶ εἰ θύρα ἐστίν, διαγράψωμεν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν σανίδα κεδρίνην.
vulg: si murus est aedificemus super eum propugnacula argentea si ostium est conpingamus illud tabulis cedrinis
clem: Si murus est, dificemus super eum propugnacula argentea; si ostium est, compingamus illud tabulis cedrinis.
kjv: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

wlc: עָנָה דוֹדִי וְאָמַר לִי קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃
lxx: Ἐγὼ τεῖχος, καὶ μαστοί μου πύργοι· ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτῶν ὡς εὑρίσκουσα εἰρήνην.
vulg: ego murus et ubera mea sicut turris ex quo facta sum coram eo quasi pacem repperiens
clem: Sponsa Ego murus, et ubera mea sicut turris, ex quo facta sum coram eo, quasi pacem reperiens.
kjv: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

wlc: כִּי־הִנֵּה הַסְּתוֹ עָבָר הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף הָלַךְ לוֹ ׃
lxx: ἀμπελὼν ἐγενήθη τῷ Σαλωμὼν ἐν Βεεθλαμών· ἔδωκεν τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ τοῖς τηροῦσιν, ἀνὴρ οἴσει ἐν καρπῷ αὐτοῦ χιλίους ἀργυρίου.
vulg: vinea fuit Pacifico in ea quae habet populos tradidit eam custodibus vir adfert pro fructu eius mille argenteos
clem: Chorus Fratrum Vinea fuit pacifico in ea qu habet populos: tradidit eam custodibus; vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos.
kjv: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.

wlc: הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ וְקוֹל הַתּוֹר נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ ׃
lxx: ἀμπελών μου ἐμὸς ἐνώπιόν μου· οἱ χίλιοι Σαλωμών, καὶ οἱ διακόσιοι τοῖς τηροῦσι τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ.
vulg: vinea mea coram me est mille tui Pacifice et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus eius
clem: Sponsa Vinea mea coram me est. Mille tui pacifici, et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus ejus.
kjv: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

wlc: הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטָה פַגֶּיהָ וְהַגְּפָנִים סְמָדַר נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ קוּמִי לְכִי רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי־לָךְ ׃ ס
lxx: Ὁ καθήμενος ἐν κήποις, ἑταῖροι προσέχοντες τῇ φωνῇ σου· ἀκούτισόν με.
vulg: quae habitas in hortis amici auscultant fac me audire vocem tuam
clem: Sponsus Qu habitas in hortis, amici auscultant; fac me audire vocem tuam.
kjv: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear it.

wlc: יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַרְאִינִי אֶת־מַרְאַיִךְ הַשְׁמִיעִינִי אֶת־קוֹלֵךְ כִּי־קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵיךְ נָאוֶה ׃ ס
lxx: Φύγε, ἀδελφιδέ μου, καὶ ὁμοιώθητι τῇ δορκάδι ἡ τῷ νεβρῷ τῶν ἐλάφων ἐπὶ ὄρη ἀρωμάτων.
vulg: fuge dilecte mi et adsimilare capreae hinuloque cervorum super montes aromatum
clem: Sponsa Fuge, dilecte mi, et assimilare capre, hinnuloque cervorum super montes aromatum.]
kjv: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.

wlc: אֶחֱזוּ־לָנוּ שׁוּעָלִים שׁוּעָלִים קְטַנִּים מְחַבְּלִים כְּרָמִים וּכְרָמֵינוּ סְמָדַר ׃
דּוֹדִי לִי וַאֲנִי לוֹ הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים ׃
עַד שֶׁיָּפוּחַ הַיּוֹם וְנָסוּ הַצְּלָלִים סֹב דְּמֵה־לְךָ דוֹדִי לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעֹפֶר הָאַיָּלִים עַל־הָרֵי בָתֶר ׃ ס
